speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; to begin our assessment, is the sensation of spinning constant or does it come in episodes? Does the spinning worsen when you move your head, stand up, or roll over in bed?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Given the sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes and the return to baseline, this is highly suggestive of a posterior canal otolith stone dislodgement. Would you like me to order a Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirmation or proceed with a visual field assessment to rule out central causes?
